annualKpiNote: Census beds = monthly average of beds available for midnight occupancy (excludes day-care, emergency, dialysis and observation beds); total beds = installed beds at year end. Occupancy = occupied beds ÷ census beds. ARPOB = hospital revenue (IP + OP, excluding OPD pharmacy and other income) ÷ occupied bed-days, so FY26 hospital revenue = 614,973 × ₹66,550 = ₹4,093 cr, which equals the AR's IP ₹3,387 cr + OP ₹706 cr. FY22-23 occupancy computed from the deck's occupied and census beds (deck rounds to 60%/59%).

clusters.def: Cluster 1 (called 'mature' until FY26) = Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi; Cluster 2 ('developing') = Lucknow, Patna, Noida. Cluster income is 'total income' (incl. some other income); group corporate costs are all loaded on Gurugram (Cluster 1).
clusters.src: Q4FY26 presentation pp. 20-21; AR FY26 p.15; Q1FY27 presentation pp. 15-16; Q4FY26 call (Lucknow + Patna occupancy 68%, Patna ~70%)

noida.facts: 550 planned beds; 433 installed at Jun-2026 (323 census, 110 day-care); 14 OTs commissioned on day one; 250+ doctors incl. 40 directors; all major insurance and PSU empanelments done; CGHS empanelment May-2026. Occupancy 'around 30%' (May-2026) and '30% to 40%' (Jul-2026). Hospitals of this kind break even at 40-45% occupancy (CEO).

cash.note: Company cash includes bank deposits under other financial assets (₹89 cr at Mar-26 beyond Screener's ₹1,130 cr cash and ₹3 cr investments). accounting.basis: Ind AS, consolidated; one reportable segment (healthcare services). Subsidiaries: Global Health Patliputra (Patna, 100%), GHL Pharma & Diagnostic (retail pharmacy and labs, 100%), GHL Hospital Ltd (South Delhi, 50% with control; DLF holds the other 50%), a medical-education foundation and patient-welfare trust.
accounting.ebitdaBases: Company EBITDA (₹1,056 cr FY26, 23.4% of total income) is before ESOP cost (₹38 cr) and includes other income (₹99 cr). Screener and the model use operating profit after ESOP and before other income (₹930 cr, 21.1%; the AR P&L gives ₹919 cr). Brokers (PL, Choice) use ₹919 cr. All are post-Ind AS 116: lease rent of ~₹47 cr a year is not in EBITDA.
accounting.grants: EPCG (export promotion capital goods) duty saved on imported equipment is treated as a government grant and released to 'other operating revenue' as export obligations (foreign-exchange earnings from international patients) are met: ₹55.8 cr in FY26 vs ₹16.2 cr in FY25, after the licences moved to the listed company on the merger. ₹77.8 cr of deferred grant income remained at Mar-2026.
accounting.doctors: Retainer doctors are paid 'retainers and consultants fee' (₹658 cr, 14.9% of FY26 revenue) on top of employee cost (₹1,096 cr incl. ESOP): together 39.8% of revenue.
accounting.exceptional: FY25: stamp duty on the MHPL merger −₹49.9 cr. FY26: EPCG interest reversal +₹19.6 cr, stamp duty reversal +₹16.0 cr, Labour Codes −₹36.6 cr (net −₹1.0 cr). Screener folds exceptional items into other income in its quarterly table.
accounting.capitalisation: Interest and directly attributable costs of projects are capitalised until hospitals open (note 6(iii)); once Noida opened (Q2-Q3FY26) its loan interest moved to the P&L: finance cost was ₹26.7 cr in Q1FY27 vs ₹13.8 cr a year earlier.
accounting.receivables: Trade receivables ₹411 cr at Mar-26 (34 days of revenue) from ₹292 cr (29 days): CGHS and insurer dues rose with volumes; ₹15.3 cr written off in FY26.
accounting.src: AR FY26 consolidated notes 2, 6, 16, 26-28, 32-36, 46; Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations
